paper.title: Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning
paper.file_name: 33_Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning.pdf
paper.research_summary: This paper develops machine learning models to predict the experimental bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites using 227 experimentally measured bandgap values collected from 1254 publications. It evaluates 24 model variants across 4 databases and 6 algorithms, identifies Xgboost and MLP as top performers, validates predictions against new experimental synthesis and DFT calculations, and uses SHAP to interpret chemical composition effects—finding B-site metal and X-site halogen ions dominate bandgap control, consistent with B–X bond length and angle physics.

tasks.objective: To accurately predict the experimental bandgap values of ABX3-type perovskites for solar cell device design
constraints: model must be interpretable via SHAP
predictions must align with physical mechanisms (B-X bond length/angle)
input_requirements: chemical composition descriptors: A-site cations (Cs+, MA+, FA+), B-site metals (Pb2+, Sn2+), X-site halogens (I−, Br−, Cl−)

evidence.text: The accurate bandgap prediction of perovskites has great significance for solar cell devices.

to establish and identify 4 models from 24 kinds of ML models. The results of the models achieve high accuracy with root mean square error (RMSE) of down to 0.55 and meanwhile, the pearson correlation coefficient of up to 99%.
We collected experimental data of bandgaps from published papers, and established four kinds of BPM(ABX3-type perovskites, all-inorganic perovskites, hybrid organic perovskites, Tin-free perovskites)

stages.stage_goal: Acquire experimentally measured bandgap values for ABX3-type perovskites from literature

evidence.text: we collect 227 sets of experimental bandgap data of perovskites from the latest 1254 publications
The first step is to search articles by using the keyword “perovskite bandgap” in the web of science according to relevance, and then download them in ACS, nature, science, wiley, Elsevier and other.

stages.stage_goal: Construct and clean a database of perovskite compositions and corresponding experimental bandgaps
stage_output: cleaned training dataset (204 samples) and test dataset (23 samples)

evidence.text: The second step is the establishment and cleaning of the database. First, data with the same chemical composition and bandgap are removed, but due to the different conditions and environments of the experiments, there will be data with the same chemical composition (input data) but different bandgap values (output data). In order to ensure the authenticity of the data and avoid the non-uniform distribution of the data, we choose to keep them in the training dataset.
We set up a training dataset and a test dataset of ABX3-type perovskites containing 204 and 23 data to train and evaluate the pros and cons of the algorithm.

stages.stage_name_raw: generation of 24 candidate bandgap prediction models
stages.stage_goal: Generate multiple candidate ML models by combining 4 databases and 6 algorithms
stage_input: six ML algorithms: LR, KNN, SVR, RF, MLP, Xgboost

evidence.text: By testing 24 kinds of BPMs generated by 4 kinds of databases and 6 kinds of algorithms, the data relevance and the accuracy of the models are guaranteed.

We use six ML algorithms by Scikit-learn and Xgboost modules to build BPMs on the pycharm platform. Linear regression (LR): ... K-nearest neighbors (KNN): ... Support vector regression (SVR): ... Random forest (RF): ... Multilayer Perceptron (MLP): ... Xtreme Gradient Boosting (Xgboost): ...

stages.stage_name_raw: model optimization via GridSearchCV and 10-fold cross-validation
stages.stage_goal: Optimize hyperparameters of each candidate model to maximize performance

evidence.text: For the above models, we optimize the models by adding “GridSearchCV” and “10-fold cross-validation”, in order to find the hyperparameters that make the model optimize the best performance.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluation using RMSE and Pearson correlation coefficient
stages.stage_goal: Quantitatively assess prediction accuracy and correlation between predicted and experimental bandgaps
stage_output: RMSE and r values for each model

evidence.text: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) is the most commonly used evaluation indicator for ML model which measures the deviation between the observed value and the predicted value. In this statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r) is often used to represent the correlation between two variables, which we use to test the performance of ML models.
Xgboost has a degree of dispersion similar to the experimental value, the lowest RMSE, and the highest correlation coefficient, so Xgboost performs best in this set of data.

stages.stage_name_raw: selection of best-performing models per perovskite subclass
stages.stage_goal: Select top-performing models for each perovskite subclass (ABX3, all-inorganic, hybrid, tin-free)
stage_output: final selected models: Xgboost for ABX3/all-inorganic; MLP for hybrid/tin-free

evidence.text: Then we use the training dataset of all-inorganic perovskite (Table S3) and the training dataset of Tin-free perovskites (Table S7) to train BPM (algorithm is Xgboost), and the test dataset of organic hybrid (Table S6) to test the BPM (algorithm is Xgboost).

After optimization, Xgboost performed best in all-inorganic perovskites data, with RMSE and r values of 0.028 eV and 0.99, respectively. MLP performes the best in hybrid perovskites and Tin-free perovskites data, with RMSE and r values of 0.016eV, 0.99 and 0.038eV, 0.99, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: validation via synthesis and optical measurement of new perovskite
stages.stage_goal: Experimentally synthesize a novel perovskite and measure its bandgap to validate model predictions
stage_output: experimental bandgap (1.61–1.62 eV) vs. predicted (1.60 eV)

evidence.text: To verify the accuracy of our ML model and predication ability for new perovskites, we synthesize the Cs0.05(FA0.85MA0.15)0.95Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3 perovskite thin films for bandgap determination. ... The bandgap of the present perovskite thin films is in a small variation range of 1.61–1.62 eV. According to the predication of our ML model (BPM-ABX3-type perovskites), the obtained bandgap value is 1.60 eV ... which has a difference with the experimental value less than 1.2% relative.

stages.stage_goal: Compare ML predictions against density functional theory (DFT) calculations for unseen compositions

evidence.text: We have also conducted the comparison with the DFT calculations on the bandgap values of the perovskites with 3 different compositions, which are new to our ML model. The prediction result of ML and the comparison are shown in Table S12. It is found that the bandgap values obtained by ML model are very close to the values of the DFT calculations.

As shown in Tables 2 and 3, for the bandgap calculation of MASnxPb1-xI3, the RMSE between the predicted ML value and the experimental value is 0.049 eV; the RMSE between the calculated DFT value and the experimental value is 0.052 eV. For the bandgap calculation of CsPb(BrxI1-x)3, the RMSE of the predicted ML value and the experimental value is 0.08 eV, and the RMSE of the calculated DFT value and the experimental value is 0.105 eV.

stages.stage_name_raw: SHAP-based interpretation of feature contributions to bandgap
stages.stage_goal: Quantify and explain how each chemical composition (A/B/X site) contributes to bandgap prediction using SHAP values
stage_output: SHAP importance ranking showing B-site metal and X-site halogen dominate

evidence.text: our ML models give the effect of each chemical composition constituting the ABX3-type perovskites on the bandgaps by using the SHAP value, and they can be well explained in physics.

Through the further analysis of the SHAP plot, we can see that the bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites can be effectively reduced with the increase of I and Sn, while the bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites can be effectively increased with the increase of Br and Pb.
